note: A curated, additive layer over existing hand-authored question items (data/hand_authored_questions.json) -- maps a subset of item_id values to the single real, identifiable misconception a wrong answer on that item most likely reflects. Deliberately NOT baked into hand_authored_questions.json itself: that file's schema and its own provenance tests are unrelated to this feature, and every tag here was written by reading that item's actual distractors, not invented from the competency_id alone. Only items where the wrong options represent one clear, defensible misunderstanding (not just a recall gap) are tagged; most items in the bank are not tagged at all, and that's fine -- services/adaptive_diagnostic.py treats an untagged wrong answer as carrying no misconception signal rather than guessing one. Most tags here are honestly single-item (a narrow, specific misconception); two are broader categories genuinely shared across multiple real items (sampling-design-tradeoff-confusion, dpdp-definition-scope-underestimation) -- grouped only where the items truly share one underlying misunderstanding, not to inflate apparent coverage.
